subject: SKU bridge, feature fencing, and upgrade path for mid-tier move
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SKU bridge & feature gating question

Hi Olga,

Quick question as we evaluate moving from Compact Tier to Mid-tier next month: will the SKU bridge allow us to flip individual features on/off while the upgrade is processing? Our product team wants to enable some Mid-tier features for a small internal pilot without fully committing to the larger capacity and we'd like to avoid a full downgrade/upgrade cycle if the pilot doesn't perform.

Specifically:
- Is there an option to enable feature-level gating (per-route or per-team) immediately after upgrade?
- What does proration look like if we move mid-billing period — is it a prorated charge or a full month charge with a credit?
- If we ask for a temporary opt-in to select features, can that be reverted without impacting our billing/seat counts?

We're trying to put together a short mutual action plan and need this to advise execs. If you can share a quick matrix of what is toggled vs what requires full SKU movement that would be ideal.

Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product Ops, BrightLane

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.io>
Date: 2026-06-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU bridge & feature gating question

Samir — thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front: yes, and it depends. Longer explanation below and a suggested playbook.

High level:
- Feature fencing: We can enable most Mid-tier features behind feature flags scoped to routes or API keys. That lets you run a limited internal pilot immediately after the upgrade without switching plans back and forth.
- Billing/proration: Upgrades mid-cycle are prorated by default (you pay the pro-rated difference for the remainder of the billing period). We can offer a one-time credit applied to the prorated amount as part of the negotiation.
- Revert path: Turning flags off does not change seat counts or capacity reservations; only changing the subscribed SKU does. So you can safely flip features for a pilot.

I've attached a quick feature-fence matrix and a draft SOW with a recommended canary approach (see attachments). Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT to review the matrix and the mutual action plan.

If you want a pricing concession for the initial month (to offset risk), tell me what target you'd like and I'll loop finance. Our typical concession for pilots is a one-time credit or a small percentage discount on the prorated portion.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: feature-fence-matrix.xlsx (matrix showing which features can be gated), BrightLane_SOW_v1.pdf (draft scope for pilot)

Date: 2026-06-07T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: SKU bridge & feature gating question (BrightLane) — pricing ask

Olga — thanks for the context. Approve a one-time credit up to 12% of the prorated delta for this pilot without needing exec sign-off (finance can absorb up to that level for strategic pilots). If the customer pushes for a larger ongoing discount we need a written request and an amendment.

Details:
- One-time credit: up to 12% applied to the prorated upgrade invoice.
- No change to monthly list pricing or renewal terms unless they sign a 12+ month commitment.
- If they convert to Mid-tier permanently within 90 days, we can extend a conversion credit (to be negotiated separately).

Ben — please document this as a concession in HubSpot and flag for future audit.

-Markus
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
